Compared per pair: the whole object word by word (pointers into the fixtures normalised to names), the guards, the constructor return value (this), the task type through GetTaskType instead of the vtable pointer, the reference lists of the fake ped and vehicle, hashes of the fake ped and vehicle (m_pReferences masked), the fake subtask contents, the 155 animation blocks (hash before and after), the four hand model reference counts, CTaskComplexPlayHandSignalAnim::ms_animBlock, the game clock and the call trace. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address, at the DLL entry and at the DLL body, so these helpers get NO credit: CBaseModelInfo::RemoveRef (decrements the counter at +8; the TXD counter is not touched) and CStreaming::RemoveModel. Not stubbed (run for real, though not validated here): CAnimManager::RemoveAnimBlockRef, GetAnimationBlockIndex("gangs"), CVehicle::SetHasslePosId, RegisterReference/CleanUpOldReference and the base class constructors/destructors. Limits: word 0 (vptr) of the task objects is excluded from the compared state (constructors compare GetTaskType instead; destructors receive the EXE vtable and the vptr rewritten by the destructor is not compared); the destructor return value is not compared (undefined in the EXE); the deleting-destructor/operator delete path is not exercised (destructors are called in place); the fake subtask has a traced slot-0 destructor and trapped other slots; float arguments include 0, -0, +-Inf, quiet NaN, a denormal and large values but never a signalling NaN; entities are zeroed fake CPed/CAutomobile buffers (vehicle byte 0x51B random); no real peds, vehicles, pools or files. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 512: position vector from finite values and special floats (0, -0, +-Inf, quiet NaN, 1.0, a denormal, FLT_MAX), time from {0,1,-1,600,INT_MAX,INT_MIN,-600} or random, two more ints (0..7 and 0..23 in 75% of cases, else random), clock from special values or random; checks m_fTime = clock + time. functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game (original with the hook off vs candidate with the hook on), 2304 isolated CPU pairs for 4 functions, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored, per-function coverage thresholds met. CAEAudioHardware::Initialise runs on a FAKE 0x1100-byte CAEAudioHardware (pseudo-random fill per case, identical in both passes); the real AEAudioHardware is never touched. DirectSoundCreate (EXE IAT 0x85801C target) and DirectSoundCreate8 (DLL import) are patched in dsound.dll only during the call and return a fake COM device (QueryInterface/AddRef/Release, GetCaps, SetCooperativeLevel and GetSpeakerConfig with scripted HRESULTs and capabilities); the real device is never opened. operator new (EXE 0x82119A, to which the DLL one forwards) is patched only during the call and hands out blocks of a 1 MiB arena pre-filled with 0xCD (other threads are forwarded to the original), so the REAL constructors of the loaders and channels run (EXE vs DLL) and are compared block by block (offset, size, FNV hash; the vtable pointer, dword 0, of the channel blocks of size 0x90 and 0x60098 is masked). Compared for CAEAudioHardware::Initialise: return value (AL), hash of the whole fake object, arena blocks, arena bytes used, the fade-thread buffer count (0xB610E8), the user-track scan state (0xB6B988) and the trace of every stubbed call with normalised arguments. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address and at the DLL body, so these helpers get NO credit: CAEAudioHardware::InitDirectSoundListener, CAEMP3BankLoader::Initialise, CAEMP3TrackLoader::Initialise, CAEStreamingChannel::Initialise, CAEAudioChannel::SetVolume, CAEUserRadioTrackManager::ScanUserTracks and Initialise, CAESmoothFadeThread::Initialise and Start, CAEStreamThread::Initialise and Start, CAEAudioHardware::LoadSoundBank and LoadSound, CAEAudioUtility::GetRandomNumberInRange<int>, CAESoundManager::AreSoundsOfThisEventPlayingForThisEntity and CancelSoundsOfThisEventPlayingForThisEntity; IsForegroundApp parks the real streaming thread during the bench. No audio thread is created or started. Declared limits: (1) after a stubbed MP3 bank or track loader Initialise returns false the DLL writes an NOTSA_LOG_ERR message (spdlog allocates through operator new) that the EXE does not have; from that point the trace, the block list and the arena usage are frozen (Freeze()), so allocations or stubbed calls made by the DLL after that failure are not detected through those channels, only through the object hash, the return value and the compared globals; (2) the path with m_nUserTracksScanState == IN_PROGRESS (Sleep(100) loop) is not tested, scan states used are OFF, COMPLETE, ERROR, 4, -1 and INT_MAX; (3) DirectSoundCreate is replaced by a fake COM device, so the real DirectSound behaviour is not exercised; (4) the constructors of channels and loaders run for real (EXE vs DLL) but are not validated here and are only compared as a side effect. Source corrected to what the EXE does before this run: CAEAudioHardware::Initialise uses operator new(0x6E4) plus Constructor() for CAEMP3BankLoader (the EXE only writes 0x14 and 0x66A, 0x4DFB10); CAEFrontendAudioEntity::Initialise writes the fields that were missing (0x80, 0x82=0x1C, 0x7E=-1, 0x84..0x94) and LoadSound takes a signed byte id (movsx). An earlier run (20261009-005347-353159, probe 17c9d956...) failed with 341 differences in 1536 CAEAudioHardware::Initialise pairs, all of them only in arena_used, blocks and recs (the NOTSA log allocations of limit 1); it is kept rejected as hashes only. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 1536: DirectSoundCreate HRESULT E_FAIL (1/8), S_FALSE (about 1/7) or S_OK; SetCooperativeLevel HRESULT 0x88780078 (1/8), S_FALSE or S_OK; GetCaps E_FAIL (1/4) or S_OK with random DSCAPS; random speaker config; dwFreeHw3DAllBuffers cycling {0,1,0x17,0x18,0x19,0x1F,0x30,0x3F,0x40,0x41,0x1000,0xFFFFFFFF} around the 0x18/0x40 thresholds; listener, bank loader and track loader initialise success 7/8 each; auto-scan byte 0, 0x80 or 1; scan state {0,2,3,4,-1,INT_MAX}; random initial fade count. Coverage in the approved run: 777 cases reach CAEStreamThread::Start (759 stop earlier), 573 with hardware mixing (>= 0x18) and 204 without, ScanUserTracks reached in 529.

Declared limits: (1) after a stubbed MP3 bank or track loader Initialise returns false the DLL writes an NOTSA_LOG_ERR message (spdlog allocates through operator new) that the EXE does not have; from that point the trace, the block list and the arena usage are frozen (Freeze()), so allocations or stubbed calls made by the DLL after that failure are not detected through those channels, only through the object hash, the return value and the compared globals; (2) the path with m_nUserTracksScanState == IN_PROGRESS (Sleep(100) loop) is not tested, scan states used are OFF, COMPLETE, ERROR, 4, -1 and INT_MAX; (3) DirectSoundCreate is replaced by a fake COM device, so the real DirectSound behaviour is not exercised; (4) the constructors of channels and loaders run for real (EXE vs DLL) but are not validated here and are only compared as a side effect. functions.scope: Simple pair bench (original with hook off vs candidate with hook on), 3840 isolated CPU pairs for 7 functions of CTaskSimpleFightingControl (3) and CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit (4) with a loaded save game, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, layout ok, saves unchanged, configs restored. Fixtures: peds, target entity, vehicles, intelligence, player data, fake tasks (traced vtable) and a fake event (traced vtable with priority and type) in private buffers with raw EXE offsets; x87 forced to 24 bits. Compared: return value, full memory of the tested object, new pool tasks (type + words without vptr), memory of the fake tasks, fingerprint of every buffer (references masked), reference lists before and after deletion, the full trace (order and number of virtual calls and rand calls), x87 control word and empty x87 stack (FpuTag); pool m_LastFreeSlot and the 0xCD fill of free slots, patched entries, vtable slots and the time step are checked at start and restored at the end. Traced stubs, patched at the EXE address and at the DLL body and acting only on the bank thread, so these helpers get NO credit: rand 0x821B1E, FindPlayerPed 0x56E210, CPedGeometryAnalyser::ComputeEntityBoundingBoxPlanes 0x5F3660, ComputeEntityHitSide 0x5F3AC0, IsPlayerOnAMission 0x464D50, IsCoopGameGoingOn 0x441390. Run for real: FindTaskByType, GetSimplestActiveTask, GetTaskFighting, GetVehicleAppearance, IsUpsideDown, IsOnItsSide, Normalise, the task pool (tasks created by Clone are found in the pool and deleted) and references. Limits: the ProstituteSolicit destructor runs with FindPlayerPed returning null when the pool tasks created by Clone are deleted (early exit), so that deletion only proves the pool ends clean; CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit::Clone with a null client is NOT tested (the EXE and DLL constructors dereference the client). GetTaskPool/IsFreeSlotAtIndex/GetAt and the 0x80 per-slot offsets are copied from TasksBatch4. CTaskComplexProstituteSolicit: no source changes. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 1024 (EXE 0x624B50): return values -1,0,3,7,8,9,10 observed, angle boundaries (+y axis, exact subtraction), wraps, rand with controlled low bits, extreme time steps (5e8: 32-bit overflow, negative, 0) and vehicles with fixed planes (sum-order sensitive mode); source changes listed above.

functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game (original with hook off vs candidate with hook on, hooked in CGame::Process), 6336 isolated CPU pairs for the 15 functions, zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same fixture from the same seed in both legs and compares the result, the fixture state (hash or bytes), the x87 control word (24-bit precision) and the ordered trace of every outgoing call with raw arguments; the hook jump state is checked. CRoadBlocks: the global block 0xA43438..0xA43C78 is saved/restored; ThePaths areas 61 (unloaded), 62 and 63 are replaced by fake nodes (0x1C), navigation links and CCarPathLink (0xE) with pointers and m_anNumAddresses restored; fake 0xA40-byte entities with a fake vtable (slot 0 = traced deleting destructor). CPools: the object pool pointer (0xB7449C) is swapped for a fake 4-slot pool of 0x19C bytes and restored. CIdleCam: fake 0x9C-byte object with guards and a fake 0x300-byte camera; CPad 0, CTimer, the gIdleCam ticker, the InterestingEvents byte, the active camera of TheCamera and CWorld::pIgnoreEntity are saved/restored. Traced stubs, which get NO credit: FindObjectsIntersectingCube, CWorld::Remove/Add, CanBeDeleted of vehicle/ped/object, rand (0x821B1E) and CGeneral::GetRandomNumber (same sequence), FindPlayerWanted/Vehicle/Coors/Ped, CreateRoadBlockBetween2Points (trace only), CWorld::ProcessLineOfSight, CProjectileInfo::RemoveIfThisIsAProjectile, CObject::operator new and constructor, the EXE printf (0x821982; the DLL does not call it, so CheckPoolsEmpty is compared by state only: nothing must change), RegisterReference, CleanUpOldReference and GetIsLineOfSightClear. Only the own part of each function is validated. Bench noise declared: CIdleCam::SetTarget with denormal floats (SSE DAZ/FTZ in the DLL vs x87 in the EXE) fails only when m_Target is null and a component is a small integer (denormal) added to 0.0; the camera vectors are normalised in the fixture (FillIdle) so no denormals reach the function. Excluded from the bench and NOT credited: CRoadBlocks::Init, CRoadBlocks::GenerateRoadBlockPedsForCar, CPools::Initialise, ShutDown, Save, Load, LoadPedPool, LoadObjectPool and LoadVehiclePool, CIdleCam::FinaliseIdleCamera, ProcessSlerp, ProcessTargetSelection, Run and Process, and the whole of CCam. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 64.

functions.source_provenance: Exact compiled TaskWave2A probe (ASI/PDB hashes in build-manifest.json); sources hashed from the probe build manifest; full 12736-row log reaudited offline and preserved gzipped with the original hash. TaskComplexKillCriminal and TaskComplexKillPedOnFootArmed (cpp and h) were corrected to the EXE before the run (uncommitted at the time).
functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the class hooks off vs candidate with the hooks on), 12736 isolated CPU pairs for 21 functions of CTaskComplexKillCriminal (8), CTaskComplexKillPedOnFootArmed (8) and CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot (5 of 10), zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, layout check ok, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture in both legs (peds incl. a full CCopPed, criminal, partner, extras, group leader, vehicles, intelligence, player data, fake group with the leader at +0x28, fake tasks with a traced vtable (GetSubTask, GetTaskType, MakeAbortable, destructor) and quiet ones, a fake event with a traced vtable, raw EXE offsets) and compares: return value, the whole memory of the tested object (and of the second object, the partner KillCriminal task), new tasks created in the task pool (type + words without vptr), fake task memory, a fingerprint of all buffers (references masked), reference lists before and after deletion, the full trace (order and count of virtual calls, rand and collaborators), the x87 control word (24-bit precision, sqrt at 24 bits) and an empty x87 stack. Traced stubs, which get NO credit: rand (0x821B1E) and CGeneral::GetRandomNumber, CPed::SetCurrentWeapon(type), SetPedDefaultDecisionMaker, CCarCtrl::JoinCarWithRoadSystem, CPed::Say, CPedGroups::GetPedsGroup, CWorld::GetIsLineOfSightClear, CPed::GetTransformedBonePosition, CCover::FindAndReserveCoverPoint and FindCoordinatesCoverPoint, CPed::ReleaseCoverPoint, CPedIntelligence::SetTaskDuckSecondary, CTaskSimpleDuck::SetDuckTimer and ControlDuckMove, CTaskSimpleUseGun::ControlGunMove, CTaskComplexKillPedOnFootArmed::CreateSubTask (validated separately; returns a marked fake task), CCamera::Using1stPersonWeaponMode and ClearPlayerWeaponMode, CWeaponEffects::ClearCrossHair and CAnimManager::BlendAnimation; for CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot::ProcessPed the five out-of-bench functions it calls are simulated with traces (which one is called and with what arguments). Run for real, not credited: IsPlayer, RegisterReference/CleanUpOldReference, CCopPed::AddCriminalToKill/SetPartner, CPedIntelligence::FindTaskByType/GetTaskDuck/GetTaskUseGun, CTaskManager::GetTaskSecondary, CPedGroupMembership::GetLeader, CWeapon::IsTypeMelee, CWeaponInfo, CVector::Normalise, CTimer, the task pool and the constructors/destructors of the subtasks created by KillCriminal (EnterCar, CarDrive, LeaveCar, GangDriveBy, KillPedOnFoot) on a full-size fake vehicle. CGame::currArea (0xB72914) and CLoadMonitor::m_eProcLevel (0xB7298C) are changed during LineOfSightClearForAttack and restored. Limits: of CTaskSimplePlayerOnFoot only 5 of its 10 functions are in the bench; OUT of the bench and with NO credit: PlayerControlDucked 0x687F30, PlayerControlZelda 0x6883D0, PlayerControlZeldaWeapon 0x687C20, ProcessPlayerWeapon 0x6859A0 and PlayIdleAnimations 0x6872C0 (they run the real player pad, camera, animation manager/IK, weapon system and crime reporting; ProcessPed only simulates them with traces). The vptr (word 0) and the return value are masked in the constructors and destructors (the task type through GetTaskType is compared instead of the vptr; the destructor return value, EAX, is undefined in the EXE; the final vptr of the destructor is the EXE base vtable vs the DLL one): this applies to the constructors/destructors of the bench, in particular those of CTaskComplexKillCriminal. Bench fixtures corrected after the first run (bench fixes, not source fixes): KC_ABORT now has the cop registered at +0x10 (before it stayed 0xCDCDCDCD and the EXE dereferenced it in CCopPed::AddCriminalToKill) and P_CLUMP uses a fake clump. The bytes +0x1B..+0x1D of KillCriminal and +0x31 of KillPedOnFootArmed are not written by the EXE constructors, so the comparison depends on the 0xCD fill of the pool slots and of the object buffer. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source corrected to what the EXE does before the approved run (uncommitted at the time; see reversing/TaskWave2A/README.md for addresses): see source_corrections_before_run. FIX_BUGS branches removed from the tested functions. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 256; source corrected: ped type filter >= 24 (any MISSIONn) cancels the criminal (0x68BEE7); the reference is registered only if the filters pass; +0x1B..+0x1D are not written. Compared type, not vptr.

functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the class hooks off vs candidate with the hooks on), 18496 isolated CPU pairs for 54 functions of CAEScriptAudioEntity (8), CAEPoliceScannerAudioEntity (13), CAEPedAudioEntity (15) and CAEStreamingChannel (18), zero differences, natural completion event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture in both legs (fake entities, fake CAEStreamingChannel of 0x60098 bytes, fake ped/physical/matrix, 8 fake CAESound, fake decoders and FAKE DirectSound/FXParamEq COM objects with own vtables; no audio singleton is touched) and compares: return value, the hash of the object under test, the hash of the physical/ped/sounds/destination buffer, the hash of the 0x60 bytes of scanner globals (0xB61CF8), the full trace of collaborator calls with arguments, the x87 control word (24-bit precision) and the restored globals (volume table 0xBD00F8 replaced by a fake and restored). Traced stubs, which get NO credit: IsSoundBankLoaded, LoadSoundBank, CAESoundManager::{CancelSoundsInBankSlot, AreSoundsPlayingInBankSlot, AreSoundsOfThisEventPlayingForThisEntity(AndPhysical), CancelSoundsOwnedByAudioEntity, RequestNewSound}, CAESound::{RegisterWithPhysicalEntity, StopSoundAndForget, SetPosition}, GetRandomNumberInRange<int>, FindPlayerPed, ReportFrontendAudioEvent, IsLoadingTuneActive, CAESmoothFadeThread::{RequestFade, CancelFade}, CAEAudioChannel::{SetFrequency, SetOriginalFrequency}, CAEAudioUtility::GetCurrentTimeInMS, CAETwinLoopSoundEntity::{Initialise, PlayTwinLoopSound, UpdateTwinLoopSound, StopSoundAndForget} and, only where the tested function calls them, ProcessMissionAudioEvent, PlayResidentSoundEvent, PlayLoadedDialogue and the Handle* of CAEPedAudioEntity. All of it on FAKE DirectSound COM; the real streaming thread is parked in IsForegroundApp during the whole bench. Limits: constructors/destructors (Script::Constructor, Scanner::Constructor/Destructor, Streaming::Destructor) mask the vptr and the CAEAudioEntity base part (m_Entity, m_tempSound), because the EXE writes only +0x10 of m_tempSound while the DLL zeroes all of it through the shared base class; the rest is compared byte by byte. The SoundDigest of sounds passed to RequestNewSound masks padding/stack garbage (+0x55, +0x40..0x4F, +0x5A..+0x5B, +0x6A..+0x6B, +0x72..+0x73). CAEStreamingChannel::InitialiseSilence with a failing CreateSoundBuffer is NOT tested (the DLL writes NOTSA_LOG_WARN, the EXE does nothing). CoInitialize (IAT 0x858350) is stubbed only during Streaming::Initialise. CAEStreamingChannel::Destructor is tested with m_pDirectSoundBuffer always non-null (the EXE does not check for null). AddFX: the eqFail fixture only fails the 2nd iteration (if the 1st failed the EXE would use an uninitialised local). Domains: sampleId 0..3, m_pPed non-null except in AddAudioEvent, non-zero channel frequencies, FillBuffer with a decoder that always advances, finite floats (no NaN/sNaN), surfaces 0..179 read from the real g_surfaceInfos (read only). Only the own part of each function is validated. Source corrected to what the EXE does before the approved run (uncommitted at the time; see reversing/AudioWave2/README.md for addresses): see source_corrections_before_run. Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Function-specific: Corpus 256; source corrected: 0x4EC168 clears m_Physical (+110h), not m_Entity (+4).

Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture (seed = case index) in both legs and compares the return value, the bytes of the fake objects, the touched global ranges, the x87 control word (24 bits) and the whole trace of doubled collaborators with raw arguments; foreign threads ignored. Traced doubles get NO credit. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source tested == current working tree at registration (class sources match the probe build manifest). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Limits: GXT texts well formed (every '~' closed, the EXE does not check NUL); GetRadioStationNameKey only with ids 0..13; StartRadio only with ids >= 0; Shutdown with a FindTxdSlot double that always returns a valid slot (the SafeRemoveTxdSlot(-1) branch is out); LoadFontValues with font id 0 or 1, complete sections and no real file (DATA\FONTS.DAT replaced by fixture lines); floats without signalling NaN; the real AERadioTrackManager is never touched, a fake 0x370-byte object is used; audio, CTxdStore, CFileMgr, CSprite2d, CStats, RNG and other collaborators doubled with trace (no credit). Function-specific: Corpus 64; source reviewed against the EXE and corrected before the run where needed (see the bank README, section on source fixes); fake object with 16-byte guards plus hashed global regions.

Evidencia limitada a los fixtures del banco, no integración universal ni independencia transitiva del EXE. Alcance por función en README del banco. Sonda compilada desde el worktree D:/Original/wq-f (HEAD 98286d43c + fusión de CQuaternion; ver artifacts/build-manifest.json) con las fuentes actuales de Pickups.cpp/.h (CPickups::GenerateNewOne ahora envoltorio de GenerateNewOne_ExeAbi). Los hashes de tested_sources son los del HEAD 98286d43c compilado; el árbol principal tiene además trabajo sin commit del lote 27 (sin validar) que modifica GangWars.h y GroupEventHandler.cpp, por lo que esos archivos no coinciden con el árbol de trabajo actual (el registro los marcará distintos hasta que ese trabajo se confirme o se descarte).

functions.source_provenance: Exact compiled PickWeap1 probe (ASI/PDB hashes in build-manifest.json); class sources hashed from the probe build manifest and equal to the working tree at registration; full 11020-row log reaudited offline in streaming and preserved gzipped with the original hash.
functions.scope: Simple pair bench inside the full game with a loaded save (original with the function hook off vs candidate with the hook on), 11020 isolated CPU pairs for 60 pending functions of CPickups, CWeapon, ALL pairs equal, pair counts equal to the bank table, passed=true globally, natural "complete" event with state_restored, saves unchanged, configs restored. Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture (seed = case index) in both legs and compares the return value, the bytes of the fake objects, the touched global ranges, the x87 control word (24 bits) and the whole trace of doubled collaborators with raw arguments; foreign threads ignored. Traced doubles get NO credit. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source tested == current working tree at registration (class sources match the probe build manifest). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Limits: CWeapon::Fire compares al!=0 (the EXE returns a garbage raw bl, 0x742794/0x7429FB, the DLL returns bool); fake pickup pool at 0x9788C0 (copied and restored), fake weapons/peds/vehicles and temporary swaps of Players[0].m_pPed, camera matrix, vehicle pool, pellet col data, g_fx.m_GunShell and ModelInfo, always restored; fixtures do not make the EXE read uninitialised locals; padding and uninitialised bytes masked. NOT covered by the bank and NOT registered: CWeapon::FireSniper, DoBulletImpact, TakePhotograph, FireInstantHitFromCar2, GenerateDamageEvent, FireProjectile, DoWeaponEffect, FireOneInstantHitRound, ProcessLineOfSight and CPickups::Update (real event group, bullet array, FX systems, real pools and world; see the bank README). Function-specific: Corpus 128; source reviewed against the EXE and corrected before the run where needed (see git diff); fake pickup pool (0x9788C0) copied and restored, fake weapons/peds/vehicles; float literals read from the EXE with std::bit_cast; fsin/fcos/fpatan by __asm.

Each case rebuilds the same deterministic fixture (seed = case index) in both legs and compares the return value, the bytes of the fake objects, the touched global ranges, the x87 control word (24 bits) and the whole trace of doubled collaborators with raw arguments; foreign threads ignored. Traced doubles get NO credit. Only the own part of each function is validated. Source tested == current working tree at registration (class sources match the probe build manifest). Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Padding and uninitialised bytes masked. Bank limits (PopFinal4): CPed::operator new (0x5E4720), CVehicle::operator new (0x6E2D50) and CTask::operator new (0x61A5A0) return holes of own buffers filled with 0xCD (fake buffers, not real pool objects); the constructors of CCivilianPed (0x5DDB70), CCopPed (0x5DDC60), CEmergencyPed (0x5DE340) and CAutomobile (0x6B0A90) are doubled in the EXE and in the DLL (they set only the fields read afterwards: vtable, model, type, intelligence, matrix, clump type 2), so they get no credit; stack tasks and events are REAL (EXE and DLL constructors/destructors) with CTaskManager::SetTask (0x681AF0) and CEventGroup::Add (0x4AB420) doubled and traced (type and words written; unwritten 0xCD arena bytes masked; in events only the fields 0x10/0x12/0x14/0x18 and 0x1C/0x20 of the attractor); world, camera, ground, collisions, paths, weapons, intelligence, streaming and the CPopulation functions each case does not test are doubled with traces and get no credit; ThePaths and the sector lists 0xB992B8 (3072 bytes), pool headers and every touched global are backed up and restored per case; CMatrix::operator* and CPed::SetHeading run undoubled (identity matrices / ped without matrix). Fixture domain: model ids 0..319 only (PedMICanBeCreatedAtThisAttractor reads [mi+0x28] without a null check, 0x61120C); PopulateInterior numPeds <= 6 (the EXE dereferences the ped returned by AddPed without a null check, 0x6165A2); the 2D effect is of attractor type (EFFECT_ATTRACTOR=3). Limits are declared per function in the function-specific scope and in the bank README. Function-specific: Corpus 256; sector lists 0xB992B8 and pool headers backed up and restored; model infos fake (ids 0..319); FindObjectsInRange/ProcessColModels/collision collaborators doubled with trace.

Historical evidence approved with explicit limits; no current dependency accreditation. Bank limits (VehModelInfoFinal4): static fake world (model infos with the EXE vtable, CVehicleStructure in a fake pool at 0xB4E680, fake TXD 0xC8800C, clumps with type byte 2, frame trees, atomics, geometries, meshes, materials and textures; plugin offsets read from the EXE); traced stubs at the EXE address and at the DLL symbol for RenderWare primitives, CFileMgr/CFileLoader, CTxdStore, CModelInfo::GetModelInfo, random numbers (0x821B1E + CGeneral::GetRandomNumber), operator new/delete, CTimer, scratchpad, the CClumpModelInfo base and the class subfunctions inside CreateInstance/SetClump, none of which gets credit. Masked: SetCarCustomPlate (the EXE passes SetupClump a dword with garbage in the 3 high bytes; only the low byte is traced); SetupCommonData pool byte 0x11 (m_DealWithNoMemory) and the DLL 0xFD filler are not compared (header and states only); the fake CVehicleStructure pool storage is zeroed before SetClump. Evidencia limitada a los fixtures del banco, no integración universal ni independencia transitiva del EXE. Alcance por función en README del banco.
